program_name: Corporate Communication and Public Relations (in English) — listed in the Italian catalogue as "Corporate communication and public relations", the English-language parallel course of the Italian twin degree "Comunicazione d'impresa e relazioni pubbliche (in Italian)"
teaching_language: Fully English-taught. It is the English-language course of the L-20 degree, symmetrical in objectives and content to the Italian twin course "Comunicazione d'impresa e relazioni pubbliche", but administered as a separate degree course with its own places quota, its own admission test in English and its own test calendar. The admission test itself is taken in English ("La prova si svolge in lingua inglese"). Note that IULM still expects non-native Italian speakers enrolled on the course to obtain proof of Italian-language ability by the end of their studies, and Italian B1 certification (if held) is uploaded during test registration — but Italian is not a barrier to admission.
campus: Milan (single campus), Via Carlo Bo 1, 20143 Milano — Faculty of Communication
academic_requirements:
Selective, capped-number admission ("corso ad accesso programmato con verifica selettiva delle conoscenze") based on a merit ranking.

PLACES: 260 places for A.Y. 2026/2027, deliberated by the Academic Senate on 4 November 2025 and confirmed on the course's own registration page. [uncertain] The English-language site page for this course instead displays "places available 500", which contradicts both the official admission-procedures PDF (260) and the Italian-site course page (260); the 260 figure from the Rector-approved procedures document should be treated as authoritative. The Italian twin course has a separate quota of 480 places.

PRIOR QUALIFICATION — eligible candidate categories are: Italian or EU nationals holding an Italian 5-year high-school diploma or an equivalent qualification; Italian or EU nationals with a qualification equivalent to the Italian diploma obtained after no fewer than 12 years of schooling; non-EU nationals, upon submission of an admission application under the rules on entry, stay and enrolment of international students and after evaluation of documentation and of the specific situation; Italian citizens attending the fourth or fifth year of an Italian high school; Italian citizens in the third or fourth year of Italian 4-year secondary courses (MD 567/2017); EU or non-EU nationals attending the final year of high school in their home country or a Foundation Year (preparatory course for international students who have not completed 12 years of schooling), subject to document evaluation. Holders of an equivalent (including four-year, EQF level IV) qualification must verify its validity with the awarding institution.

RANKING CRITERIA: 50% admission-test result + 50% school record. For candidates holding the diploma or in the fifth year of high school, the school-record half is 25% third-year average marks + 25% fourth-year average marks. For candidates in the fourth year, the whole 50% is the third-year average. For candidates in the fourth and final year of 4-year secondary courses (or graduates of them), it is 25% second-year + 25% third-year averages; for those in the third year, the whole 50% is the second-year average. Marks for physical education, civic education, religion and conduct are excluded, and the average is rounded to one decimal place.

SCORE THRESHOLDS BY SESSION: in the 1st session only candidates scoring at least 70% of the maximum are admitted. In the final session all candidates are admitted by ranking until places are filled; those below 70% may be admitted with Additional Learning Obligations (OFA), which must be cleared by the end of the first year (September 2027), and the Faculty Board may still set a minimum score below which a candidate is not ranked. For the 2nd and 3rd sessions either the 1st-session or the final-session criteria are applied depending on remaining places, and the criterion chosen is published on the University website 5 days before the test date.

WAITING LIST: candidates in excess of the places available are put on a waiting list keeping their ranking position; ties are broken by scholastic merit. Ranking scrolling starts from 21 April 2026 (2nd session), 16 June 2026 (3rd session) and 28 August 2026 (4th session); waiting-list candidates called up normally have no more than three working days to confirm.

FOREIGN QUALIFICATIONS: Italian or foreign applicants permanently resident abroad holding a foreign qualification obtained abroad must apply through apply.iulm.it so IULM can verify the validity of the qualification before they may sit the test; non-validity precludes admission and the test fee is not refunded. Applicants resident in Italy holding a foreign/international school qualification obtained in Italy upload their full transcript and diploma in the online procedure for the same verification. Attendance at a foreign school, or a certified semester of the fourth year abroad, counts as an element of merit in the ranking. Enrolled holders of a foreign qualification must later produce a Statement of Comparability and/or CIMEA verification, or a Dichiarazione di Valore.

OTHER: first-year transfers from other universities are not normally permitted for selective-admission courses; transfers into the second and third year are possible subject to assessment by the Registrar's Office (ammissioni.triennali@iulm.it). It is not possible to register in the same session for both this course and its Italian twin, since they are the same course in two languages.
language_requirements:
ENGLISH — B2 CEFR is a hard prerequisite for admission to the test, not merely for enrolment: "candidates must have a knowledge of English equivalent to at least level B2 in the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR)".

Route 1 — certificate: candidates holding an accepted international certificate obtained after 1 January 2024 are admitted directly to the admission test; a digital copy must be attached during online registration. Accepted certificates and minimum scores: IELTS 5.5; Cambridge FCE or CAE and Linguaskill 160; BEC Vantage 160; Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language grade C; TOEFL iBT 72; Pearson PTE 46; Trinity College London ISE II.

Route 2 — IULM assessment test: candidates without a valid certificate must sit IULM's own Oxford English Test (Use of English + Listening), free of charge, on the dates in Annex 2 of the admission procedures. Reaching B2 or above in BOTH the Use of English and the Listening Comprehension sections admits the candidate to the admission test. A pass at B2 or above obtained in an earlier session (not before 1 November 2023) also counts.

Failing the assessment test: candidates who do not reach B2 may instead be admitted, at no extra fee, to the admission test for the Italian-taught twin course. They may also retake the assessment test in later sessions at no additional cost; if they later pass it, they must still sit the English-course admission test — a test already passed for the Italian twin course does not carry over.

Exemption: applicants who completed their entire high-school studies at English-speaking schools in Italy or abroad may be exempt from the assessment test.

ITALIAN — no Italian certificate is required for admission. During test registration, non-native Italian speakers applying to this course are asked to upload "any Italian language certification for at least level B1" (optional). After enrolment, non-native Italian speakers on this course (or those without Italian at least B1) will be given procedures for obtaining, by the end of their studies, the required proof of ability to use Italian effectively. Note that the compulsory second-year "English for Corporate Skills" course and the post-enrolment Oxford Placement Test described in section 3 of the procedures apply to the Italian-taught courses, not to this English-taught one.

entry_exam_or_test:
Online selective written admission test, invigilated remotely.

Stage 1 (only for candidates without a valid B2 certificate) — Oxford English Test / language assessment test: sections Use of English + Listening, 45 questions, 73 minutes, provided free of charge. B2 or above in BOTH sections is required to be admitted to Stage 2. (Note: the course registration page states 70 minutes for this test while the official admission-procedures PDF and the Italian course page state 73 minutes.)

Stage 2 — admission test, taken in English: 60 questions in 50 minutes, delivered online. Subjects and question counts: text comprehension (10), English grammar (17), numerical reasoning (4), verbal critical reasoning (8), logical reasoning (11), culture of corporate communication (10). Sample questions are published by IULM as a downloadable PDF (CCPR_esempi_2026.pdf).

No interview stage is foreseen for this course (unlike some other IULM programmes).

Test fee: €110 per degree course, non-refundable under any circumstances except failure to sit the test because places were insufficient, a decision of the University's governing bodies, or invalidity of the admission qualification. Non-payment or late payment precludes access to the test. Candidates who fail a session may re-apply for a later session in the same academic year without paying again. It is not possible to register in the same session for both this course and its Italian twin; taking the other course's test in a later session requires paying the fee again.

Logistics: candidates need a device with webcam, microphone and stable internet; a compulsory online identity verification (about 5 minutes, dates in Annex 4) must be completed before the test; the test must be taken inside the assigned virtual room started by IULM staff — tests begun early or outside the virtual room are void. Spot checks are made and anomalies (webcam off, copying, other people present, unauthorised devices) can incur score penalties or annulment of the test.

Students temporarily abroad: Italian candidates abroad for documented exceptional reasons in a time zone at least two hours from Italy may request alternative arrangements at ammissioni.triennali@iulm.it.

uncertainty_notes:
All figures are for A.Y. 2026/2027; no fallback to 2025/2026 was needed. The governing document is the admission-procedures PDF approved by the Academic Senate on 4 November 2025 and marked "rev March 2026", so details may still be revised during the cycle.

1) QUOTA CONFLICT (main open point). The English-language site page cited as official_program_url in the research brief shows "places available 500" on its registration tab, while the Rector-/Senate-approved admission-procedures PDF lists 260 places for "Corporate Communication and Public Relations (in English)" and the Italian-site page for the same English-taught course shows "posti disponibili 260". The Italian twin course is separately listed at 480. 260 has been used as the value of record. The 500 figure appears to be a stale or mis-merged number on the English-language site.

2) URL STRUCTURE. IULM's Italian site treats the English-taught course as a distinct course with its own slug — https://www.iulm.it/it/offerta-formativa/corsi-di-lauree-triennali/comunicazione-dimpresa-e-relazioni-pubbliche-cv-eng/ — while the English-language site has only ONE "Corporate Communication and Public Relations" entry, under the Italian twin's slug (comunicazione-impresa-relazioni-pubbliche), which serves English-course content (English test subjects, English-course test dates 23/03, 28/05, 15/07) but the wrong quota. No /en/ page exists for the cv-eng slug (HTTP 404 tested). The brief's official_program_url has been kept, but the Italian cv-eng URL is the more reliable page for quota and test details.

3) OXFORD TEST DURATION CONFLICT. The admission-procedures PDF (Annex 5) and the Italian course page both state the Oxford English Test is 45 questions in 73 minutes; the English-language registration page states 70 minutes. 73 minutes has been used.

4) FOURTH-SESSION TEST DATE. Annex 1 does not fix a date for this course in the 4th session: "dates to be defined according to number of remaining places (if only 4th-session applicants: 15 July 2026)". The course pages list 15/07/26. Treat as provisional.

5) CAPACITY RISK. The procedures state that extraordinary sessions may be added if places remain, but also that registration deadlines may be shortened on over-subscription and that only sessions with sufficient remaining places accept applications. Whether the course is still open in a given session is not published in advance; applicants should check before paying the €110 fee. International (non-EU abroad) sessions 5–7 explicitly run only "subject to places still being available".

6) DUAL DEGREE. Dublin Business School (Honours Bachelor Degree in Marketing) and Royal Roads University are named as dual-degree partners on the course page, but no separate admission requirements, selection procedure or quota for the dual-degree tracks could be found on iulm.it; the tracks appear to be selected during the course rather than at admission. Not fully captured.

7) APPLICATION FEE FOR INTERNATIONAL APPLICANTS. The prerequisites page says non-EU applicants abroad "Pay an application fee in order to start the evaluation" on apply.iulm.it, but no amount is published there; the €110 test fee in the procedures PDF explicitly carries a footnote that a different rate may apply to candidates sitting the test abroad. The exact apply.iulm.it fee is not published on iulm.it.

8) ENGLISH SECTION 3 SCOPE. Section 3 of the procedures (post-enrolment compulsory Oxford Placement Test and the "English for Corporate Skills" course requiring B1+) explicitly lists the Italian-taught courses, not this English-taught course; it has therefore been excluded from language_requirements for this programme, but the PDF's wording is ambiguous enough that it is worth re-checking.

9) Fields left with no per-programme value: none. campus and degree_class are taken from the Italian course page; no building-level teaching site beyond the single Milan campus (Via Carlo Bo 1) is published.
